beats.say: Here is an animal cell, drawn as if it were sliced open.
Its edge is the cell membrane, a thin skin that decides what comes in and what goes out.
Inside is the cytoplasm, a crowded gel where the cell does most of its work.
The nucleus holds the cell’s DNA, and the dark spot within it, the nucleolus, builds ribosomes.
And the mitochondria turn sugar and oxygen into the energy the cell spends.

beats.show: Membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria: the parts every animal cell shares.
